Thanks Laura — uploading the register now. Snapshot of current renewal risk items (quick summary):

1) SLA credit request / latency tail behavior — RISK LEVEL: HIGH (Owner: Rishi)
   - Issue: Over the last 30 days Zephyr saw 3 P95 spikes affecting batch reporting jobs (impacting revenue recognition).
   - Mitigation: Propose 10% invoice credit and prioritized dedicate patching schedule; alternative: offer a temporary dedicated capacity pool for scheduled jobs.
   - Exec ask: Approve up to 10% credit or sign-off on Dedicated pool budget to avoid renewal pushback.

2) SOC2 scope & attestation timeline — RISK LEVEL: MEDIUM-HIGH (Owner: Monica / Security)
   - Issue: Zephyr requested an in-scope-only report for select subsystems and an accelerated timeline that may not align with our audit window.
   - Mitigation: Offer scoped attestation for data flows affecting Zephyr, plus a letter of attestation for remaining items.
   - Exec ask: Approve constrained audit effort and sign-off on a letter of attestation.

3) Pricing & Discounting mismatch — RISK LEVEL: MEDIUM (Owner: Tessa)
   - Issue: Procurement is pushing for a larger multi-year discount tied to usage commitments.
   - Mitigation: Structured discount tied to Dedicated capacity commit + usage tiers; hold final approval pending finance/AR review.

I've attached a filled tab in Renewal_Risk_Register.xlsx with the above items marked and mitigation owners. Marked SLA credit as RED since it needs a finance/exec decision before we get to the QBR.

On the logistics side — recommend we keep the customer-facing QBR to 30 minutes (exec summary + top 3 asks) and have a separate 45-minute internal review with sales + finance + product for deeper technical/contract discussion.

- Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
